rule.title: Housing Stability Notification Act notice requirement
rule.requirement: A landlord planning to end a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to quit or non-renewal, and must also submit the Notice to Quit / Non-renewal of Lease Submission Verification Form to the City.
rule.coverage_conditions: All landlords planning to end a tenancy agreement, and foreclosing owners, must provide the notice and submit the verification form to the City.
rule.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; non-profit facilities whose primary purpose is short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse.
rule.penalty: Violations are enforced by Inspectional Services; 1st offense a warning, 2nd and subsequent offenses $300 per day. Failure to submit the required information may result in a fine up to $300 per day.
rule.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.

sources.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.

The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.

rule.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rule.requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding or land, or with BPDA income-restricted units, may not blanket-deny applicants with arrests or convictions; they must screen case-by-case, disregard non-convictions, sealed, expunged and juvenile records and convictions over 5 years old, and not use credit scores.
rule.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rule.exemptions: Where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others; current criminal behavior.
rule.interaction: Yields to federal or state criminal history requirements that conflict with this policy.
rule.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rule.quoted_span:
will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on 
a case-by-case basis.
rule.conflict_note: The policy states that where federal or state law imposes a conflicting criminal history requirement, that law preempts this policy.

rule.title: Boston Fair Housing Regulations source-of-income protection
rule.requirement: In Boston, a landlord may not refuse to rent to someone because they use rental assistance, including Section 8, social security disability, and veterans vouchers.
rule.coverage_conditions: All housing rented, bought, sold, or financed in the City of Boston.
